Default tiers of a pyramid set

Source: R/set.R
a5_pyramid_set_tiers.Rd

The tiers a5_write_pyramid_set() uses when none are given: from the leaves down, three LODs a tier, each with shard resolution 12 below its finest LOD, and every remaining LOD in one tier with shard resolution 0. Tiers that would hold none of the levels are left out. For leaves at resolution 18 the tiers are LODs 16 to 18 (shard resolution 6), 13 to 15 (3) and 2 to 12 (0).

Usage

a5_pyramid_set_tiers(data_resolution, lods = NULL)

Arguments

data_resolution

The leaves' resolution.

lods

The coarser LODs. Default: every resolution from 2 up to data_resolution.

Value

A data frame with one row per tier, in ascending LOD order: lod_min, lod_max, shard_resolution, tile_size and row_group_size (NA: one tile a row group).

Examples

a5_pyramid_set_tiers(18)
#>   lod_min lod_max shard_resolution tile_size row_group_size
#> 1       2      12                0     16384             NA
#> 2      13      15                3     16384             NA
#> 3      16      18                6     16384             NA
a5_pyramid_set_tiers(16, lods = c(4, 8, 12, 14))
#>   lod_min lod_max shard_resolution tile_size row_group_size
#> 1       4      10                0     16384             NA
#> 2      11      13                1     16384             NA
#> 3      14      16                4     16384             NA
